text: BPAL (Bulk Procurement and Logistic Management System) is an integrated software and hardware system developed by CDCorp. It is designed to automate and manage the raw material supply chain for industries such as pulp, paper, bioenergy, and recycling. BPAL connects administrative software with physical hardware (like truck scales, gate readers, and dumpers) to create a contactless, automated workflow for receiving bulk materials. Its main goals are to reduce operational costs, eliminate human error, ensure worker safety, and provide real-time business intelligence. whats new ? you can check the whats new tab and see what are the new feture included.

It does not close the application window, only the active session. - Use Case: Use this when you are finished working but want to leave the application open for another user to log in. 2. OPTION: Security Lockout - Location: File > Security Lockout - Function: Locks the application interface instantly. - Behavior: Hides the current screen contents and requires a password to resume. - Use Case: Use this when stepping away from your desk (e. g. , for lunch or a break) to prevent unauthorized access without fully logging out. 3. OPTION: User Properties - Location: File > User Properties - Function: Opens the configuration window for the currently logged-in user. - Behavior: Displays a dialog box containing user details (permissions, username, preferences). - Use Case: Use this to view account details or modify specific user settings. 4. OPTION: Log Files > - Location: File > Log Files - Visual Indicator: Contains a right-facing arrow (>), indicating a sub-menu. - Function: Accesses the system's history and error tracking logs. - Behavior: Hovering over this item will reveal a secondary list of specific log types. - Use Case: Used for troubleshooting errors or auditing system history. 5. OPTION: Exit F12 - Location: File > Exit F12 - Shortcut Key: F12 - Function: Closes the BPAL Administration application completely. - Behavior: Terminates the software. - Use Case: Use this when you are completely done with the application and wish to close it on your computer. # Product Notebook Interface - Detailed Guide ## Overview The Product Notebook is a data entry and management interface used to create, view, and edit product information in the BPAL system. This document explains the field types, functionality, and user interactions available in the notebook. --- ## Field Types and Visual Indicators ### Open Fields (White Background) Fields with a white or light background are available for data entry. Users can click on these fields and input or modify information. These fields are editable and can receive user input. **Example:** The "Code" field, description fields, and the "Type" field in the product notebook are typically open fields ready for user input. ### Closed Fields (Gray Background) Fields with a gray background are locked and cannot be edited. These fields are read-only and display information that is either system-generated, auto-populated, or intentionally restricted from user modification. Users cannot enter or change data in closed fields. **Example:** Fields that display calculated values, status fields, or fields managed by system rules may appear grayed out. --- ## Field Icons and Their Meanings ### Magnifying Glass Icon (Lookup Table Field) The magnifying glass icon indicates that the field has a lookup table associated with it. This is standard functionality in BPAL for fields with this icon. **Functionality:** - Clicking on the magnifying glass icon opens a lookup dialog or dropdown menu - The lookup table contains a predefined list of valid values for that field - Users can select an appropriate value from the list instead of typing it manually - Lookup fields ensure data consistency and prevent invalid entries - The lookup helps users find and select the correct code or value quickly **Example:** The "Type" field in the product notebook has a magnifying glass icon, allowing users to browse and select from available product types like "BROWNGRADE". ### Information Icon (Circular "i" Icon) Located to the right of the magnifying glass icon, this circular icon with the letter "i" provides quick access to additional information related to the code field.

Helps users understand what each code represents without leaving the notebook - Provides context-sensitive help and reference information **Example:** Clicking the "i" icon next to a product type code would display the full definition, properties, and other details about that product type. --- ## Tabs and Sections The Product Notebook includes multiple tabs for organizing different types of information: ### Available Tabs - **Properties:** Contains basic product information such as code, description, category, and type - **Scaling:** Manages size, weight, or dimension scaling parameters - **Test:** Contains testing criteria and quality assurance information - **Other:** Miscellaneous additional product information and properties - **Delivery Point:** Information related to delivery locations and logistics - **Product Group:** Classification and grouping information for the product - **Unit Of Measure:** Definition of measurement units used for the product - **Audit:** Historical tracking and audit trail information about product changes Each tab organizes related fields logically, allowing users to navigate between different categories of product information. --- ## Field Components - This allows the user to choose between saving changes or discarding them. - **Behavior - If No Changes Were Made:** If no data has been changed in the notebook, pressing the Cancel button or the X in the top right corner will close the notebook immediately without any user confirmation prompt. - **Use When:** You want to exit the notebook. If you have made changes, you will be prompted to save or discard them. If you haven't made changes, the notebook closes immediately.

" - User options: - **Save:** Saves all changes and closes the notebook - **Don't Save:** Discards all changes and closes the notebook - **Cancel:** Returns to the notebook to continue editing **Scenario 2: User Made No Changes and Presses Cancel or X** - The notebook detects that no data has been modified - The notebook closes immediately without any confirmation prompt - No dialog appears - the action is instantaneous ### X Button in Top Right Corner The X button in the top right corner of the notebook window behaves identically to the Cancel button: - If changes were made, it triggers the confirmation dialog - If no changes were made, it closes the notebook immediately ### Why This Matters This change detection feature protects users from accidentally losing work. By prompting for confirmation only when changes exist, it also prevents unnecessary dialogs when simply reviewing data without making edits.

Open the Product Notebook 2. Navigate to the appropriate tab (Properties, Scaling, Test, etc. ) 3. Locate the open (white background) field you want to edit 4. Click on the field and enter or modify the data 5. If the field has a magnifying glass icon, click it to select from a lookup table 6. Click **Apply** to save and continue editing, or **OK** to save and close ### To View Additional Details About a Selection 1. Click the magnifying glass icon to open the lookup table 2. Select the desired value 3. Click the circular "i" icon next to the field 4. Review the information popup that appears 5. Close the popup and proceed with your work ### To Discard Changes 1. Click the **Cancel** button 2. All unsaved changes will be discarded 3.
